assertions.object_key: {"content":"Implemented email demo and card-style HTML export, published as live page. 183 tests green, conformance unchanged at 47.","type":"commit"}

object_value.content: Implemented email demo and card-style HTML export, published as live page. 183 tests green, conformance unchanged at 47.

source_refs.excerpt:
email demo + card-style HTML export, published as a live page

A visitor clicks one URL and sees a matter ledger distilled from a pile of
emails — nothing to install.

- mh export --format html renders one self-contained file (all CSS/JS inline,
  zero external requests, light/dark, mobile-readable): an overdue-first
  commitments strip, a responsive card grid of matters with micro-labeled
  facts and collapsible evidence timelines, a by-person view, and visible
  ✏️ human-correction badges. Card layout replaced the first draft's dense
  full-width stack after review. Overdue is judged against --as-of (default:
  the scope's max recorded_at, stated in the footer) so identical state
  renders byte-identical HTML — golden-hash tested, along with a
  no-external-request test and an every-anchor-resolves test.
- adapters/email_mbox.py maps mbox/EML to Records: Message-ID identity,
  In-Reply-To/References threading, bulk/auto-submitted mail filtered, loud
  failure on missing ids. Quote-chain stripping, HTML bodies and signature
  removal are marked TODO, not silently attempted.
- examples/email/demo.mbox: an 18-message fictional vendor project staged to
  show four moments — a delivery date slipping twice (three due_at segments),
  a decision reversal, an owner handoff (filed as origin=human corrections,
  which doubles as the correction-protocol showcase), and a commitment still
  overdue, red at the top. Synthetic emails have no real permalink, so
  evidence links jump to a rendered source-email appendix — every link on the
  page works for an anonymous visitor.
- Published: docs/demo/email-ledger.html and docs/demo/self-ledger.html (the
  dev ledger through the same renderer, regenerated nightly by ledger.yml),
  cross-linked via the new --related footer option; GitHub Pages serves
  /docs; README (EN/zh) opens with the live-demo links.

Verified: 183 tests green (wide and narrow terminal), ruff clean, conformance
unchanged at 47; the email chain ran end to end on a real gateway with the
gate rejecting five out-of-bounds candidates; both pages re-render
byte-identically from their stores.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

assertions.object_key: {"content":"Implemented mail connector with IMAP hub input, console panel, file upload, and hardened against real inbox. 237 tests green locally, 285 with PostgreSQL 17.","type":"commit"}

object_value.content: Implemented mail connector with IMAP hub input, console panel, file upload, and hardened against real inbox. 237 tests green locally, 285 with PostgreSQL 17.

source_refs.excerpt:
mail connector: IMAP hub input, hardened against a real inbox

mh mail setup/sync (stdlib imaplib, provider presets with app-password help
links) plus the Console Connectors panel: config persisted to matterhorn.toml
with the credential ONLY in process memory — never in toml, db, logs, or any
GET response, with redaction tests including the case where an error message
equals the credential verbatim. UID watermarks ride sync_positions with
UIDVALIDITY reset detection; auto-sync reuses the serve scheduler; the panel
shows watermark, counts, next run, and provider help on auth failures. The
console also gains file upload (.mbox/.eml/.yaml routed through server-side
detection) and a quick single-message form.

Three rounds of hardening came from pointing it at a real Gmail inbox:

- Reality round 1: an 11-minute first sync (unbounded UID 1:* pull, one FETCH
  round-trip per message) that died on the first HTML-only email. First runs
  are now bounded to the most recent initial_window (default 50) with the
  watermark set to the mailbox top, fetches are batched, HTML-only bodies are
  extracted to readable text via a stdlib parser, and a message that fails to
  parse drops alone — counted — instead of aborting the run.
- Reality round 2: 32 messages became 29 junk matters (Reddit notifications,
  newsletters, CI mail) because notification senders don't set Precedence:
  bulk. Machine mail is now filtered by List-Unsubscribe, noreply-class
  senders, and Auto-Submitted — counted by reason. Real conversations
  aggregate BEFORE extraction: References root (falling back to normalized
  subject, including 回复/转发 prefixes) becomes the thread identity, whole
  conversations reach the extractor together, and a server-derived
  subject_key stamp makes every email of a conversation land on the same
  matter across syncs — the model never chooses identity.
- mh mail reset / the panel's re-pull control clears the watermark for clean
  re-extraction comparisons.

Verified: 237 tests green locally, 285 with PostgreSQL 17, ruff clean,
conformance unchanged at 47.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

assertions.object_key: {"content":"Added a step-by-step manual for verifying the engine, including invariants from production bugs and eight judgement calls.","type":"commit"}

object_value.content: Added a step-by-step manual for verifying the engine, including invariants from production bugs and eight judgement calls.

source_refs.excerpt:
docs: hands-on acceptance manual

A step-by-step guide for verifying the engine by running it rather than by
reading the code or trusting test names. Every command and every expected
output in it was executed on a clean venv before being written down.

It walks the invariants that came from production bugs — the blocker flicker
(INV-4), the two-matters-merged-into-one card (INV-5), human precedence
(INV-9), zero-LLM reads (INV-10) — and shows what a broken result looks like,
not only a passing one. It also records the eight places where the proposal was
ambiguous and a judgement call was made, so those can be overruled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

assertions.object_key: {"content":"Implemented hub topology with MCP over streamable HTTP, single-command setup, live view enhancements, and documentation. 244 tests green locally, 292 with PostgreSQL 17.","type":"commit"}

object_value.content: Implemented hub topology with MCP over streamable HTTP, single-command setup, live view enhancements, and documentation. 244 tests green locally, 292 with PostgreSQL 17.

source_refs.excerpt:
hub topology: one service, every input converges, every consumer mounts

The mh console/serve process is now the hub: MCP over streamable HTTP mounts
at /mcp on the same port (nine tools shared with the stdio server — one
definition, two transports), the REST surface stays the browser's contract,
and the db belongs to the service exclusively; every other process goes
through REST or MCP-HTTP.

mh setup claude-code wires a project in one command: embedded mode writes the
stdio .mcp.json; --url mode writes the url-type entry plus session hooks that
POST to the hub. Hooks are fail-open by contract — two-second budget, exit 0
on any failure — and two live defects were caught during owner acceptance:
Claude Code's hook schema takes one command string (the command+args shape
would never have executed), and bare 'mh' does not resolve in hook shells, so
setup now writes the absolute path of the running executable.

Live view: the console gains a service-wide activity stream and a connections
overview (mail watermarks, per-scope ingestion, distill queue) on a five-
second poll. And because record ids are deterministic, per-turn delivery is
free: hub setups also install a Stop hook shipping the transcript tail after
every assistant turn — overlapping redeliveries dedup to nothing (verified:
two overlapping deliveries of 6 messages stored exactly 4 records, one matter
evolving across turns) — so matters appear while the conversation is still
going, not just at session end.

docs/agent-team.md (+zh) documents the topology, multi-agent scope sharing,
sender.id-as-agent-name for query_by_person, and the loopback/auth boundary.

Verified: 244 tests green locally, 292 with PostgreSQL 17, ruff clean,
conformance unchanged at 47; MCP-HTTP round-trip over the official SDK
client; hook silent-failure at 0.24s; end-to-end walkthrough accepted by the
owner (session → hub → live matters without exiting the session).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

assertions.object_key: {"content":"Proposal: spec enters repository before code, including SPEC.md and conformance suite.","type":"spec"}

object_value.content: Proposal: spec enters repository before code, including SPEC.md and conformance suite.

source_refs.excerpt:
M0: spec first — normative SPEC.md and the golden conformance suite

The proposal calls for the specification to enter the repository before any
code, because two implementations (this Python engine and an internal Java
one) must be held to one source of truth.

- spec/SPEC.md: the nine principles (P1-P9) and ten invariants (INV-1..INV-10)
  written normatively, plus the exact assertion_id derivation, projection
  algorithm, conflict-resolution order, retract guards and query semantics.
- spec/conformance/: language-neutral golden YAML cases. Every case is also
  replayed and re-ingested by the runner, so INV-2 (idempotent replay) and
  INV-3 (projection is a pure, rebuildable function) are enforced for free on
  every case rather than tested once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

assertions.object_key: {"content":"Implemented console operating surface with browse, query, correct, feed, chat features. 202 tests green locally, 244 with PostgreSQL 17.","type":"commit"}

object_value.content: Implemented console operating surface with browse, query, correct, feed, chat features. 202 tests green locally, 244 with PostgreSQL 17.

source_refs.excerpt:
console: the operating surface — browse, query, correct, feed, chat

mh console mounts a static REST client on the serve port: the product's
operator/developer/demo surface, peer to MCP/REST/CLI/SDK but itself only a
client of documented public endpoints — where the REST API lacked a
capability, the API grew (GET /v1/scopes on both stores; POST
/v1/scopes/{id}/ingest with server-side format detection for chat lines,
YAML/JSON messages, and raw email) rather than the console getting a back
door.

Five blocks arranged as the product's own pipeline — 1 produce (paste +
extract with visible gate breakdown, offline sample via the fixture provider),
2 memory (matters and detail; every current value carries a first-class
Correct affordance that files an origin=human assertion with traceable
source), 3 consume (a host-side tool-use chat whose only tools are the five
deterministic queries through the same service layer REST uses, evidence chips
under every answer; plus the query workbench with human/raw views). Without
an LLM key the chat hides and everything else works.

Live DeepSeek testing hardened the chat loop: invalid tool arguments return
to the model as tool results instead of failing the turn, hitting the
tool-call cap forces a final no-tools answer instead of an error, and tool
descriptions state that list_matters already carries current values so models
stop fishing per-predicate. A Postgres-only DISTINCT/COLLATE error in
list_scopes was caught by the dual-backend run.

The visual language is the ledger-paper direction chosen from three designed
candidates: double-rule masthead, ruled-paper feed, stamp badges, italic
correction links, red-ink human annotations; sepia dark variant; loopback
bind by default.

Verified: 202 tests green locally, 244 with PostgreSQL 17, narrow-terminal
green, ruff clean, conformance unchanged at 47.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

console: the operating surface — browse, query, correct, feed, chat

mh console mounts a static REST client on the serve port: the product's
operator/developer/demo surface, peer to MCP/REST/CLI/SDK but itself only a
client of documented public endpoints — where the REST API lacked a
capability, the API grew (GET /v1/scopes on both stores; POST
/v1/scopes/{id}/ingest with server-side format detection for chat lines,
YAML/JSON messages, and raw email) rather than the console getting a back
door.

Five blocks arranged as the product's own pipeline — 1 produce (paste +
extract with visible gate breakdown, offline sample via the fixture provider),
2 memory (matters and detail; every current value carries a first-class
Correct affordance that files an origin=human assertion with traceable
source), 3 consume (a host-side tool-use chat whose only tools are the five
deterministic queries through the same service layer REST uses, evidence chips
under every answer; plus the query workbench with human/raw views). Without
an LLM key the chat hides and everything else works.

Live DeepSeek testing hardened the chat loop: invalid tool arguments return
to the model as tool results instead of failing the turn, hitting the
tool-call cap forces a final no-tools answer instead of an error, and tool
descriptions state that list_matters already carries current values so models
stop fishing per-predicate. A Postgres-only DISTINCT/COLLATE error in
list_scopes was caught by the dual-backend run.

The visual language is the ledger-paper direction chosen from three designed
candidates: double-rule masthead, ruled-paper feed, stamp badges, italic
correction links, red-ink human annotations; sepia dark variant; loopback
bind by default.

fix(cli): honest exit-code contract and a terminal correction path

Both defects were masked by a fabricated dependency: a previous build could not
download Typer and installed a 103-line hand-written stub into the venv under
the name `typer 0.0.0+verification`. Every CLI test had been passing against
that stub. The venv has been rebuilt with real Typer 0.27.0, which is how these
surfaced.

- `mh conformance run` now exits 0 when all cases pass, 1 when cases run and
  some fail, and 2 when the suite itself is unusable. It previously raised
  click.exceptions.Exit(2), which the stub honoured and real Typer does not, so
  an unreadable suite exited 1 with a traceback. This command is the CI gate and
  the harness the internal Java implementation mirrors, so its exit contract is
  part of the deliverable, not an implementation detail.
- `mh correct` closes the one surface where the correction protocol was missing.
  P8 makes corrections a first-class part of the core contract and the proposal
  names an unused correction protocol as a top risk, yet an operator at a
  terminal had no way to file one.
- Typer and click now carry lower bounds so a fresh install cannot silently
  pick up an incompatible version.

Verified: 141 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; the three exit codes
demonstrated for real; a correction through the CLI flips a query answer from
(blocked, model) to (open, human).

source_refs.excerpt:
# Project strategy

## Layer and promise boundary

Matterhorn is a deterministic, evidence-backed temporal memory layer for
agents. Messages enter on the write side; projected matters and their history
come from persisted evidence rather than generation at answer time. The project
positions this as an L3 layer that complements broad L1 capture and retrieval
tools: Matterhorn accepts traceable upstream material and adds closed
predicates, bi-temporal assertions, deterministic projection, replay, and
first-class human correction.

Sources:
[README — project description and promise boundary](../README.md#the-promise-boundary),
[Positioning alongside L1 memory tools](../docs/positioning.md),
[SPEC — principles](../spec/SPEC.md#1-principles).

## Name and package

The public distribution name is `matterhorn-memory` on PyPI. The Python import
name remains `matterhorn`, as shown by the SDK entry point
`from matterhorn import Engine`.

Source:
[README — installation and SDK entry point](../README.md#five-minute-journey).

## Two-verb facade

The default SDK facade is deliberately centered on two verbs:
`add(messages)` for writes and `matters(scope_id)` for reads. `add()` persists a
task without calling an LLM and `flush()` runs the queued write pipeline;
`matters()` is a deterministic projected read and never calls an LLM. Direct
card and Record ingestion, detailed temporal queries, and correction remain
progressively disclosed advanced surfaces.

Sources:
[README — Two-verb SDK](../README.md#two-verb-sdk),
[README — Progressive disclosure](../README.md#progressive-disclosure),
[CHANGELOG 0.5.0](../CHANGELOG.md#050---2026-07-29).

## Thread-first identity

A communication thread is the first deterministic matter boundary. Identity
does not depend on a model choosing a subject. Cross-thread evidence merging
still obeys the evidence threshold, including the absolute rule that a single
shared source never causes a merge.

Sources:
[CHANGELOG 0.4.0](../CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-07-29),
[SPEC — evidence-based identity merge](../spec/SPEC.md#2-invariants).

## Evidence revocation, not conclusion deletion

Edited Records append new observations and assertions. Deleting or revoking a
Record does not mutate or remove the immutable assertions, intervals, or
materializations it supported. Queries keep the conclusion visible while
marking each source as active or revoked and reporting aggregate evidence
status.

Sources:
[SPEC — INV-11 immutable source lifecycle](../spec/SPEC.md#2-invariants),
[CHANGELOG 0.4.0](../CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-07-29).

## Dual-backend conformance

SQLite and PostgreSQL implement the same Store boundary. Backend-specific SQL
and value normalization stay inside the Store layer, and a behavioral
difference between the two backends is a defect. Both backends run the same
language-neutral golden conformance cases. The current public suite contains
47 cases.

Sources:
[SPEC — PostgreSQL Store and consistency boundary](../spec/SPEC.md#19-postgresql-store-and-consistency-boundary),
[SPEC — Reference conformance harness](../spec/SPEC.md#20-reference-conformance-harness),
[README — conformance suite](../README.md#the-promise-boundary).

## Current milestone

The latest release listed in the changelog is 0.6.0, dated 2026-07-29. It adds
deterministic projection-diff events, at-least-once webhook delivery, versioned
scope export/import, service-only daily UTC flushing, and four output-surface
conformance cases that bring the suite to 47.

Source:
[CHANGELOG 0.6.0](../CHANGELOG.md#060---2026-07-29).

source_refs.excerpt:
refactor: the import graph now matches the architecture

Pure refactor, zero behavior change — the layering was right but four smells
hid it, and each shared-primitive squatter created edges that made the real
structure unreadable.

- canonical.py moves to the top level: canonical_json, instant_text,
  stable_hash and the id derivations are normalization primitives, not engine
  logic. SubjectRecord moves into contracts — it is a persisted shape, i.e. a
  contract. store/, query/, distill/ and render/ no longer import engine at
  all.
- FIELD_WIDE_RETRACT moves to contracts: 'field-wide retract' is contract
  semantics; the renderer knowing an extractor-internal sentinel was the tell.
- The extractor is now an injection seam: contracts defines the
  RecordExtractor Protocol, the engine core speaks only to the Protocol, and
  the built-in MessageCardExtractor is wired in a new top-level defaults.py —
  the composition root the project brief's 'plugin, replaceable as a whole'
  always implied. matterhorn.engine keeps exporting the composed Engine via a
  lazy PEP 562 forward so public imports are unchanged.
- html/markdown renderers move under render/, with shared read-model helpers
  in projection.py.
- tests/test_architecture.py encodes the layering as a readable rules table
  and walks the AST to enforce it — the architecture is now test-enforced,
  like the invariants, rather than prose.

Verified: 232 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17, narrow-terminal
green, ruff clean, conformance 47/47 exit 0, ledger fill and both export
formats re-run, and the refactored renderer reproduces docs/demo/
self-ledger.html byte-identically.

source_refs.excerpt:
M2+M3: distillation gate, protocol surfaces, adapters, PostgreSQL and release

Write path (the only place a model is allowed to run, P1):
- LlmGateway SPI (OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic / null) behind an async dream
  queue. ingest() never calls a model; dream() drains the queue and re-projects
  inside one transaction (INV-6).
- A validation gate with named, counted rejection reasons (P3). The load-bearing
  one is SOURCE_NOT_TRACEABLE: a candidate's cited sources must be a subset of
  the originating card's evidence, so the model cannot invent provenance. The
  same traceability check backs the message->card adapter — one implementation,
  not two.
- Gated creation of non-primary child subjects, which is what makes the
  flagship profile's one semantic predicate (decision_adopted on DECISION_SLOT)
  reachable at all. Child keys are derived deterministically, so a replayed
  dream creates no duplicate subject.

Read path: MCP server on the official SDK (seven tools), FastAPI REST 1:1 with
those tools, and a Claude Skill. All three share one service layer, and none of
them can reach the distill package — enforced by an import-graph test.

Storage: a second backend. PostgreSQL exists to prove the spec is implementable
twice, so the entire conformance suite runs against both, and ordering is
pinned to bytewise (COLLATE "C" / BINARY) rather than the server's locale — a
spec whose answers depend on a deployment's collation is not a spec.

Release: adapters for ReMe/OpenViking digests, four runnable examples including
the human-correction flow, Docker, docs, and CI with the cross-backend
conformance suite as a required gate against the two implementations drifting.

Verified: 138 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17, on both C and
en_US.UTF-8 collations; mh conformance run passes 37/37 on both backends and
exits non-zero on a seeded failure.

M1: deterministic engine core, SQLite store, query family and CLI

Card-level ingest -> assertions -> intervals -> materialized memory cards,
with the read path deriving answers by query alone (P4/INV-10).

Design decisions worth calling out, each traceable to a production bug the
proposal records:

- INV-4 (blocker/next_step/due flicker): a field being absent means "no
  observation", never "cleared"; explicit clearing is expressed by
  EpisodeCard.cleared_fields. The condition that emits a RETRACT and the
  condition that updates the projection are one shared function, not two
  copies that can drift, and re-asserting the same value keeps the existing
  interval open instead of closing and reopening it.
- INV-5 (two unrelated matters merged into one card): merging requires an
  absolute floor of two shared sources; a single shared message is never a
  merge reason, no matter what share of the new card's evidence it represents.
- INV-8/INV-9: SINGLE conflicts resolve on (valid_from, origin, recorded_at,
  assertion_id) with human origin outranking model, and every resolved
  conflict is counted and reported rather than silently discarded.

The core carries no domain vocabulary: it executes any valid SchemaProfile,
and ships two genuinely different profiles (org-matters, personal-decisions)
so the abstraction is driven by more than one case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

new_value.content: Implemented hub topology with MCP over streamable HTTP, single-command setup, live view enhancements, and documentation. 244 tests green locally, 292 with PostgreSQL 17.
Implemented mail connector with IMAP hub input, console panel, file upload, and hardened against real inbox. 237 tests green locally, 285 with PostgreSQL 17.
Implemented console operating surface with browse, query, correct, feed, chat features. 202 tests green locally, 244 with PostgreSQL 17.
Refactored import graph to match architecture. 232 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17.
Implemented email demo and card-style HTML export, published as live page. 183 tests green, conformance unchanged at 47.
The internal brief is now ignored by git; SPEC.md remains the normative source.
Added a step-by-step manual for verifying the engine, including invariants from production bugs and eight judgement calls.
Fixed `mh conformance run` exit codes (0/1/2) and added `mh correct` command. 141 tests green.
Implemented distillation gate, protocol surfaces, adapters, PostgreSQL backend, and release. 138 tests green, conformance 37/37.
Implemented core engine, SQLite store, query family, and CLI. Handles invariants INV-4, INV-5, INV-8, INV-9.
Proposal: spec enters repository before code, including SPEC.md and conformance suite.
Strategy captured in devlog, covering layer boundary, naming, SDK facade, thread-first identity, revocation, dual-backend conformance, and current milestone.
